evidence: The core gates are all conditioned on cfg.rule_sets.loaded being None: factory.py:110-153 (remove_sql_modes=frozenset(), no RuleSetGuard/RefusalRedacting, allow_memory_writes unchanged, _StaticUserResolver, DefaultSystemPromptBuilder(rule_sets=False) leaves the prompt unchanged per default.py diff), query_database.py (select_rule_set, owner check and catalog check all under `if rule_sets is not None`; set_rule_set_selection(None) is inert), MySQLRunner (remove_sql_modes empty means the setup branch condition is unchanged). But preflight.py changed behavior with NO rule-set file. probe_database's MySQL branch was refactored onto mysql_connect_kwargs (src/sqllens/rule_sets.py:515-528), and this applies unconditionally. Counterexample: a `mysql://host/db` URL with no user. Config accepts it (config.py:118 checks only the scheme). Before, probe_database raised PreflightError('mysql url must include user and host'). Now the ValueError from mysql_connect_kwargs (rule_sets.py:521) is caught in preflight.py and re-raised as 'invalid MySQL URL; it must name a user and host and a numeric port'. The old text for a non-numeric port, 'invalid MySQL URL; check its format and port', is also changed. The database name parsing also moved from lstrip('/') to removeprefix('/') (rule_sets.py:287), which differs for a path like '//db'. So 'behaves exactly as before' is not literally true. The differences are error-message wording and a rare URL edge, not the query path.

src/sqllens/rule_sets.py:77-78 base class _Record sets ConfigDict(extra="forbid", strict=True, frozen=True). Every model derives from it: Binding (81), MetadataKeys (94), GlobalSwitch (115), Source (120), TableRule (168), RuleSet (188), RuleSetFile (208). So an unknown key in the file root, [binding], [metadata], [[rule_sets]], [rule_sets.source], [[rule_sets.source.global_switches]] or [[rule_sets.tables]] raises a pydantic extra_forbidden ValidationError. load_rule_sets (310-313) turns that into RuleSetFileError via _validation_problems (278-283), which prefixes each problem with _record_path(loc) (268-275). That renders loc ('binding','foo') as 'binding.foo', ('rule_sets',0,'source','foo') as 'rule_sets[0].source.foo', and ('rule_sets',0,'tables',1,'foo') as 'rule_sets[0].tables[1].foo'. A top-level unknown key renders as its bare name. Wrong values (type, pattern, min_length, the custom validators) go through the same path and name the field's position. Model-level validators (duplicates, row_rule) name the enclosing record. I traced an unknown key through each record type and found no counterexample. TOML syntax errors are reported separately by tomllib with its own position (307-308). The catalog check is a separate step and is not a file-format error.

src/sqllens/safety/rule_sets.py apply_rule_set (297-317) does no column-level checking. _analyze (162-190) and _check_reference (132-151) refuse only on table-shaped problems (unlisted table, qualifier, options, column aliases on a table, DUAL). _rewrite (219-226) replaces each listed base table with a derived table selecting only the listed columns (_derived 193-216, joins kept outside the derived table). _rewalk (259-278) only checks that tables are wrapped and no hint is left. So an unlisted column in HAVING, a window ORDER BY or USING (...) reaches MySQL unchanged. Each derived table lacks that column, so MySQL raises an unknown-column error, as the module docstring (17-19) also says. Traced inputs: HAVING col, OVER (ORDER BY col), JOIN ... USING (col), NATURAL JOIN (the hidden column is not in the derived table, so it is not matched), and a correlated outer reference (the outer table is also a derived table). None is refused by the guard for the column. A select alias with the same name as a hidden column resolves to the alias and exposes nothing hidden. The guard's KIND_* refusals contain no column-based kind.

src/sqllens/rule_sets.py:168-185: TableRule declares row_rule: Any = None and an after-mode model_validator checks `"row_rule" in self.model_fields_set`. _Record (line 77-78) config is extra=forbid, strict, frozen, with no aliases or validate_assignment, so nothing else alters fields_set. In pydantic v2, fields_set after validation holds exactly the keys supplied in the input, including an explicit null, and omitted defaulted fields are excluded. After-validators run on the built instance, so fields_set is already populated. Result: a supplied row_rule (even null) is rejected and an omitted one passes. tests/unit/test_rule_set_file.py:254-260 covers the supplied case (error names rule_sets[0].tables[0]). The omitted case is covered by the valid example_document loads.

StrictStr rejects it with a string_type error before _date runs. The test at tests/unit/test_rule_set_file.py:143-147 injects datetime.date(2026, 11, 1) and expects an error containing 'string'.
